vsam.why: base/cntl/adef121.jcl DEFINE1: DATA(... KEYS(10 0) RECORDSIZE(225 225)); the engine's facts do not read KEYS / RECORDSIZE inside the DATA component, so the case states them

scenarios.name: add-new-customer
scenarios.why: WRITE of a new key after the last record: NORMAL; the record is the 225 bytes from CA-CUSTOMER-NUM

scenarios.name: add-key-zero
scenarios.why: boundary: the lowest key 0000000000, before every existing record

scenarios.name: add-key-max
scenarios.why: boundary: the highest key and every customer field filled to its full width

scenarios.name: add-blank-details
scenarios.why: the key alone: the record is the key and 215 blanks (the INITIALIZE'd COMMAREA)

notes: GenApp's VSAM 'add customer' (LGACVS01, LINKed by LGACDB01 with the 32500-byte LGCMAREA COMMAREA): EXEC CICS WRITE FILE('KSDSCUST') FROM(CA-CUSTOMER-NUM) LENGTH(225) RIDFLD(CA-CUSTOMER-NUM) KEYLENGTH(10); on NORMAL the program GOBACKs (no RETURN command, CA-RETURN-CODE untouched). Each scenario's KSDSCUST is compared after the task. Every non-NORMAL RESP in this program goes to WRITE-ERROR-MESSAGE, whose first act is EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('LGSTSQ') (GenApp's TS/TD error logger, defined in the CSD); the equivalence harness runs one program and has no port of LGSTSQ, so a scenario that reaches it is refused (Unsupported: LINK PROGRAM(LGSTSQ)). The error paths -- DUPREC on an existing customer, NOSPACE / NOTOPEN / IOERR, CA-RETURN-CODE '80' and ABEND LGV0 -- are therefore NOT exercised here; they need LGSTSQ modelled (or ported) first. Keys: CA-CUSTOMER-NUM is PIC 9(10) in the COMMAREA, so a key mixing letters and digits cannot be passed; no browse, so no key order is exercised (the comparison sorts each side's records by key bytes). Data: ksdscust.txt is GenApp's own ten sample customers (base/cntl/db2cre.jcl's customer INSERTs), laid out as LGACVS01 writes them (CA-CUSTOMER-NUM + CA-CUSTOMER-REQUEST's first 215 bytes); CA-NUM-POLICIES is the count of that customer's rows in db2cre.jcl's policy INSERTs.
